post_research_ranking.reason: Canonical references + closure trigger + one terminal transaction is conventional, direct and likely faster for terminal reads.
Deleting writable terminal authority has a distinct invalidation/rebuildability property and can be tested cheaply.
Derived truth plus non-authoritative cache may recover most read performance without reintroducing independent semantic authority.
Factored terminality may aid recovery semantics but risks expanding surface area.
Typed proof objects overlap GAR/type-system work and should not be added until runtime/schema discriminator justifies them.

killed_or_deferred.reason: Proof/hash witness does not itself solve canonical support binding and strongly collides with prior art.
Provenance semiring machinery is disproportionate to the immediate V17 closure problem.
Session/typestate completion overlaps current ClayCode/GAR language frontier and is not the cheapest falsifier.
Potentially useful later for invalidation/history semantics, but too broad for the current minimal discriminator.

candidate_claim: Terminal DONE should be a read-only derived causal-closure proposition; any physical cache is evidence/performance state, not semantic authority.
kill_rule: Kill CCW as a distinct runtime architecture if a conventional persisted receipt with exact closure trigger and atomic transaction matches correctness/recovery and CCW's remaining benefits reduce to ordinary view/cache engineering.
